title: Tracklight | Plan the night
text: Tracklight helps railway access planners turn competing requests into reviewable weekly schedules. The planning board keeps every activity visible, shows allocated workload and highlights weeks needing attention. These are decision-support drafts, not permission to enter the railway.

title: Bring your own eight CSVs
text: Judges can upload all eight instance files through the browser. This demonstration uses a renamed copy of the public benchmark to check that scheduling does not depend on sample identifiers. It is a synthetic test, not an official hidden instance.

title: Schedule and inspect live
text: The uploaded instance is scheduled by a bounded background job. Refreshing the browser reconnects to that job. The result retains all fifty-four activities and covers the required workload. Use the timeline and activity inspector to examine allocations, deadlines and sharing.

title: Explain the contradiction
text: In the supplied example, A001 and A011 must share a night at one platform but use separate nights at another. Tracklight identifies the activities, week and locations behind that contradiction. The explanation is conditional on the disclosed full-night model.

title: Check alternatives before review
text: Find checked alternative searches for a complete replacement under the selected scenario. Independent checks run before a candidate is presented. The comparison exposes completion, delay, early closure, excess capacity and changed allocations. It also identifies unchanged inputs, rules and implementation.

title: Protect work already agreed
text: When work grows, open controlled replanning. Declare the completed weeks, lock activities that must stay fixed and enter the disruption. Here, we add one workload unit to A001, freeze weeks one through ten and lock A002. The original plan is preserved.

title: Review the consequences
text: The revised plan is checked across the entire schedule, including dependencies and sharing relationships. An independent audit verifies completed work and locks. The objective prioritises scenario cost before changed activity count. The interface reports whether that minimum-change result is proven.

title: Export reproducible evidence
text: Export the review pack to retain exact decisions, input identity, validation and planner-review evidence. A disruption pack also preserves revised inputs, its planning context and the parent. Returning to the original version keeps both versions; it does not solve the new disruption.

title: Evidence, with honest limits
text: The release contains separate A, B and C candidate CSV sets, pinned setup instructions and reproducibility records. Full protection rules and official validator acceptance remain unresolved. Tracklight makes those limits visible so a planner can distinguish checked model results from operational approval.
